messages:
anna (runtime): Quick heads-up — I'm seeing a perf regression after a driver restart + cache warm sequence.  p50 token latency climbs ~18ms -> 34ms for long-context workloads.
mike-g: ugh. is it a cold-KV issue or kernel selector fallback? :thinking:
sara_ml: do you have profile traces? could be seqlen-dependent path picking different kernels when cache miss spikes.
anna (runtime): attaching quick summary from a dev run: hit ratio dropped from 92% -> 45% after driver restart (no model change). CPU on the driver spiked, and we fell back to smaller micro-kernels for some layer types. Numbers:

- pre-restart: cache hit 92%, p50 token latency 18ms, throughput 420 tok/s
- post-restart: cache hit 45%, p50 token latency 34ms, throughput 260 tok/s

Looks like our cache keying didn't survive some runtime metadata change.
yves: did driver binary sha change? we tag cache entries with driver build id previously.
anna (runtime): driver binary is same, but runtime emitted a different config.hash after an ops reorder. The cache key schema currently uses: {model_id}:{model_version}:{config_hash}:{seqlen_bucket}:{prefix_hash}

deploy-bot: Reminder — deploys sometimes bump config.hash when config ordering isn't canonical. See infra-1234.
mike-g: hmm, that config.hash is too brittle. We should separate stable identity (model_id+model_version) from volatile runtime annotations.
sara_ml: Agreed. Proposal: switch to a two-part key: a stable namespace and a runtime fingerprint. Something like:

```
kv_key = "ns=" + stable_namespace + ":v=" + model_version + ":k=" + mutation_key
stable_namespace = hash(model_id, model_arch)
mutation_key = hash(driver_build, kernel_selector_version, canonicalized_config, seqlen_bucket, prefix_hash)
```

On lookup we prefer entries where mutation_key matches exactly; otherwise treat as miss but keep old entries under the same namespace for diagnostics.
yves: and persist old entries for a grace period? that helps rolling upgrades where we revert.
mike-g: yes, keep persistence but add metadata on each entry: {mutation_key, created_at, last_seen, source_driver, kernel_profile_tag}. That way we can auto-migrate or surface mismatches in telemetry.

anna (runtime): sounds good. Two ops questions:
1) Invalidation policy on model version bump: full namespace purge? or keep to help A/B rollback?
2) How to signal to kernel selector that a mismatch should trigger a re-autotune instead of a full fallback path?
sara_ml: for (1) I suggest: if model_version changes -> purge namespace unless model_version is a minor param (we already have variant pinning). For full model upgrade (weights change), purge.

For (2) kernel selector should consult mutation_key differences. If kernel_profile_tag differs only in kernel_selector_version, schedule an async autotune job and use best-known kernel; don't immediately fallback to the slow micro-kernel unless performance delta > threshold.
mike-g: implement a background re-autotune queue: when miss because mutation_key mismatch, push a sample request to autotune queue keyed by (model_version, kernel_selector_version, seqlen_bucket). If autotune completes, we atomically add entries with new mutation_key.
yves: operationally we need a cache-version header in the driver-runtime handshake. If driver reports cache_version != entry.mutation_key, runtime can decide whether to revalidate or invalidate existing entries. Also emit metric kv.cache_mismatch{reason} with tags.

anna (runtime): good. Also propose a TTL policy: persist entries by default for 7 days, but add a sliding last_seen for active workloads. Garbage collect entries older than 30d. And add a max-per-namespace cap so a noisy prefix can't blow memory.
sara_ml: +1. Also add seqlen bucketing rules for keys: use coarse buckets for >1024, and more granular up to 512. That reduces key explosion.
mike-g: implementation note:

```
# config snippet
kv_cache:
  persist: true
  persist_ttl_days: 7
  max_per_namespace: 20000
  seqlen_buckets: [16,64,128,256,512,1024,inf]
  key_schema: "ns:{stable_hash}:mk:{mutation_hash}:sl:{seqlen_bucket}:ph:{prefix_hash}"
```

anna (runtime): quick checklist for the patch I will open:
- update keying impl and add migration helpers (keep old entries + telemetry)
- add mutation_key metadata fields to entries
- handshake header cache_version in gRPC driver init
- autotune queue trigger on mismatch with sampling logic
- GC policy + max-per-namespace enforcement
- tests: simulate driver config reorder and model minor change

yves: pls also add a debug endpoint to list stale mutation_keys per namespace. We had that during the last incident and it saved debugging time. :+1:
mike-g: we should add a non-disruptive migration job that scans namespaces and computes stats: hits_by_mutation_key, last_seen, avg_latency. Surface it in Console.

anna (runtime): thanks team. I'll open WIP PR and link here. For the regression we saw, I re-ran with a quick revert of config canonicalization and hit ratio returned to ~90% and latency recovered. So bug confirmed.
sara_ml: awesome — let's also add a small perf test that asserts hit ratio > 80% after driver restart for staged dataset.
anna (runtime): will do. PR incoming in ~2h. tagging @mike-g @yves for review. :eyes:
